I am 65 years old and I have farmed these 20 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and calculate the cost per mu, but most of what I know comes from doing it with my own hands and watching what happens on my neighbors' fields. I do not trust new ideas unless I saw them work on someone else's land first.

My farm is 20 mu, which is bigger than most around here. I keep 15 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 5 mu in chrysanthemum. I do not change my cropping plan for no reason. Last year was decent, so this year I will do mostly the same thing, maybe adjust a little if I see the wheat coming up thin.

For the winter wheat on my 15 mu, I will plant the improved variety Jimai 22. My neighbor Lao Wang planted it last year and got over 1000 jin per mu. I will drill 30 jin of seed per mu. For fertilizer, I put 1 bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing time — that is 50 kg of 15-15-15. Then at jointing in March, I spread 30 kg of urea per mu. If the wheat looks yellow at the flag leaf stage, I add another 10 kg of urea per mu. All together that is about 20 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I would rather spend the extra money on fertilizer than risk a thin harvest. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I accept. I irrigate 3 times with my well: once before winter to help the seedlings survive, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I do rotary tillage before sowing. For sprays, I put down herbicide once after sowing, insecticide once when the aphids show up, and fungicide once if the spring is damp — 3 sprays total. I expect 1000 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For summer maize on the same 15 mu, I sow right after wheat harvest in early June. I use hybrid seed, Nongda 372, about 2.5 kg per mu. I do not till the land — I plant directly into the wheat stubble. That saves diesel and time, and everybody around here does it this way. I put 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer in the seed furrow at planting, and I topdress with 25 kg per mu of urea when the plants are knee-high. That comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. Maize needs less water than wheat, so I irrigate twice: once at tasseling and once at grain filling, if the rain does not come. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once before emergence and insecticide twice for corn borers — 3 sprays total. I expect 1100 kg per mu.

For chrysanthemum on my 5 mu, I grow it for the dried flower market. It pays better than grain but needs more fussing. I plant in April with an improved variety that the seed dealer says the buyers want. I put 3000 seedlings per mu. I use 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting — the one with more potassium. Then I topdress twice with 15 kg of urea each time. That is about 12 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium per mu. Chrysanthemum drinks a lot of water, so I irrigate 4 times through the season. The bugs love chrysanthemum leaves, so I spray 4 times: insecticide 3 times and fungicide once. I do rotary tillage before planting. I expect about 280 kg of dried flowers per mu.

I think about my whole budget. My son works in Handan city and sends money home, so I can afford the inputs on 20 mu. But I still count every yuan. I watch what my neighbors do, and most of them apply about the same amounts. I spent a lot on fertilizer last year, but the wheat price was decent. This year I will do the same. Change is risky. I know what worked before.
